# Third-party notices

<!-- Generated by scripts/third_party_notices.py. Edit the script, not this file. -->

HiWave is licensed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (`LICENSE`). The HiWave
application also contains the third-party works listed here, each under its own
licence. This file carries the copyright and permission notices those licences
require to travel with the binary. It must ship with every build that users
download.

It describes one build: `cargo build -p hiwave-app` with default features, for
`aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-apple-darwin`. How it is regenerated and
checked is in section 7 and in `docs/GATES.md`.

## Contents

1. Licences with source or file-level obligations (MPL-2.0)
2. Works that are not Cargo crates (Chart.js, Unicode CLDR data, SQLite, the Rust standard library)
3. Vendored and modified source (`third_party/`: Boa, with code ported from V8 and atoi_simd)
4. Rust crates in the dependency closure of the `hiwave` binary (385 crates), by licence, with each licence text once
5. Crates under more than one licence at once, and licence files reproduced in full
6. What is in the repository but does not ship
7. How this file was made, and what was not verified

No component of the shipped binary is under a GPL, LGPL, AGPL or SSPL licence,
and none is without a licence. Licences here that are not simple permissive ones:
MPL-2.0 (section 1), the Python Software Foundation licence stack on code
ported from V8 (section 3), and the Apple Public Source License 2.0 on
documentation comments in one crate (security-framework, section 5).

## 1. Licences with source or file-level obligations

### MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft)

- **adblock 0.12.0** (declared `MPL-2.0`). No copyright line in the published crate; Cargo.toml authors: Anton Lazarev, Andrius Aucinas. <https://github.com/brave/adblock-rust/>
- **option-ext 0.2.0** (declared `MPL-2.0`). No copyright line in the published crate; Cargo.toml authors: Simon Ochsenreither. <https://github.com/soc/option-ext.git>

  generated from the list). The list is maintained by Mozilla and its
  contributors and carries this notice: "This Source Code Form is subject to the
  terms of the Mozilla Public License, v. 2.0. If a copy of the MPL was not
  distributed with this file, You can obtain one at https://mozilla.org/MPL/2.0/."
  <https://publicsuffix.org/list/public_suffix_list.dat>,
  <https://github.com/publicsuffix/list>. The `psl` crate's own code is
  `MIT/Apache-2.0` and is listed in section 4.

What MPL-2.0 requires of us for these:

- **Tell recipients where the source is** (section 3.2(a)). The two crates are
  used exactly as published on crates.io; their source is at the URLs above and
  at `https://crates.io/crates/adblock/0.12.0` and
  `https://crates.io/crates/option-ext/0.2.0`. The Public Suffix List is
  used as the `psl` crate compiled it; the list's source form is at the
  publicsuffix.org URL above and the compiled form at `https://crates.io/crates/psl/2.1.175`.
  This file is that notice.
- **Keep their files under MPL-2.0** (section 3.1). If HiWave ever changes a file
  of either crate, or the list, the changed file must be published under
  MPL-2.0. Vendoring a patched copy the way Boa is vendored would trigger this.
- **Do not restrict the recipient's rights in that source** (section 3.2(b)). The
  binary may be distributed under other terms (HiWave's own MPL-2.0, or the
  commercial licence), but those terms cannot limit what MPL-2.0 grants over
  this source.
- **Leave their notices in place** (section 3.4).

The full text of MPL-2.0 is in section 4.

### Unicode CLDR 48 data (Unicode-3.0)

Copyright (c) 1991-2025 Unicode, Inc. All rights reserved. Distributed under
the Unicode License v3. <https://cldr.unicode.org>,
<https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr-json> (release 48.0.0),

- `crates/rustkit-bindings/src/likely_subtags.txt`: the likely-subtags table
  (`common/supplemental/likelySubtags.xml`, read from cldr-json 48.0.0
  `cldr-core/supplemental/likelySubtags.json`). Data only, re-encoded by

- `crates/rustkit-bindings/src/web_intl.js`: the first-day-of-week and weekend

  marked "CLDR en") follow CLDR's `en` locale data.

Licence text: Unicode License v3, in section 4. Several crates in section 4
that declare only MIT or Apache-2.0 also embed tables generated from the
Unicode Character Database (the `unicode-*` crates, `regex-syntax`, `idna`'s
data); where such a crate ships a Unicode licence file it is reproduced in
section 5.

### SQLite 3.46.0 (public domain)

`libsqlite3-sys 0.30.1` is built with its `bundled` feature (through
`rusqlite`), which compiles the SQLite 3.46.0 amalgamation (`sqlite3/sqlite3.c`)
into the binary. SQLite is in the public domain and asks for no notice.
<https://www.sqlite.org/copyright.html>. Its source files say:

> The author disclaims copyright to this source code. In place of a legal
> notice, here is a blessing:
>
> May you do good and not evil.
> May you find forgiveness for yourself and forgive others.
> May you share freely, never taking more than you give.

### The Rust standard library (MIT OR Apache-2.0)

The binary links Rust's `std`, `core` and `alloc` from the toolchain pinned in
`rust-toolchain.toml` (1.91.0). `cargo tree` does not list them. "Copyrights in
the Rust Standard Library are retained by their contributors" (The Rust
Project Developers, <https://thanks.rust-lang.org>); it is licensed
`Apache-2.0 OR MIT` and used here under MIT (text in section 4). The standard
library has dependencies and in-tree exceptions of its own (for example
`backtrace`, `hashbrown`, `libc`, `compiler_builtins`, Unicode data). They are
listed in the `COPYRIGHT-library.html` file that ships with the toolchain
(`$(rustc --print sysroot)/share/doc/rust/`) and at
<https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/COPYRIGHT>; they are not
reproduced here.

## 3. Vendored and modified source

`third_party/boa_engine`, `third_party/boa_parser` and `third_party/boa_ast`
started as the crates.io 0.22.0 releases of the Boa JavaScript engine (upstream
`boa-dev/boa` at `337a3668`) and are wired in through `[patch.crates-io]`.

**All three are modified by HiWave.** The changes are marked `HIWAVE PATCH (...)`
in the source and each patch is described in
`third_party/boa_engine/PATCHES.md` (which also covers the `boa_parser` and
`boa_ast` changes): a cross-thread interrupt and its follow-ups, recursion
and native-stack limits, V8's sort order, evaluation-order and
temporal-dead-zone fixes, interpreter statistics and performance paths, among
others. They are not the software Boa published; do not report their
behaviour upstream as Boa's.

Upstream licenses Boa `Unlicense OR MIT`; HiWave uses it under MIT. The
published crates contain no licence file, so the notice is given here:

    Copyright (c) 2019 Jason Williams

(from `LICENSE-MIT` in <https://github.com/boa-dev/boa> at `337a3668`). The
crates are listed again with the other MIT crates in section 4.

### Code ported from V8 into the vendored Boa

`third_party/boa_engine/src/builtins/array/v8_timsort.rs` (added by HiWave) is
a Rust port of V8's sorting built-ins:

- `third_party/v8/builtins/array-sort.tq` (`Array.prototype.sort`). V8 keeps
  that file under the Python licence stack, because it is derived from
  CPython's `Objects/listobject.c`. Its header reads: "Copyright (c) 2001,
  2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013,
  2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025,
  2026 Python Software Foundation; All Rights Reserved" (V8 `main`, read
  2026-11-14). Licence: `third_party/v8/builtins/LICENSE` in V8, the Python
  Software Foundation License Version 2 with the BeOpen, CNRI and CWI
  agreements, reproduced in full in section 5.
- `src/builtins/typed-array-sort.tq` (typed-array sort). "Copyright 2019 the
  V8 project authors. All rights reserved." BSD-3-Clause; V8's `LICENSE.v8`
  is reproduced in full in section 5.

Summary of changes, as the Python licence asks of a derivative work: the
algorithm was rewritten in Rust from V8's Torque version (itself a port of
CPython's list sort) to work on Boa's value vectors with a fallible
comparator, and arrays shorter than 8 elements go straight to binary
insertion to match Chrome's measured behaviour. <https://github.com/v8/v8>

The "join stack" change described in `PATCHES.md` matches V8's observable
behaviour and ports no V8 code.

### Code Boa itself copied

`third_party/boa_engine/src/builtins/date/utils.rs` (`mod fast_atoi`, present
in upstream Boa) says it is copied from `atoi_simd`'s `src/fallback.rs`.
atoi_simd is `MIT OR Apache-2.0`: Copyright (c) 2022 Dmitry Rodionov (upstream
`LICENSE-MIT`). <https://github.com/RoDmitry/atoi_simd>. Used under MIT, text
in section 4.

## 4. Rust crates in the dependency closure of the `hiwave` binary

Every crate `cargo tree -p hiwave-app -e normal` reports for
`aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-apple-darwin`, HiWave's own crates left out.
360 of them are compiled and linked into the binary. The other 25 are
procedural macros (marked in their entries): they run at build time and are
not linked, but the code they generate is, so they are listed too.

Where a crate offers a choice of licences (`A OR B`), HiWave uses it under the
first of these that it offers: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, BSD-2-Clause, ISC, Zlib.
The expression the crate declares is shown with each entry. Copyright lines are
copied from the licence files inside each published crate; where a crate ships
none, the entry says so and gives the `authors` field of its `Cargo.toml`
instead.

## 5. Crates under more than one licence at once, and licence files in full

These declare an `AND` expression: every licence named applies to some part of
the crate.

- **aws-lc-rs 1.18.1** (declared `ISC AND (Apache-2.0 OR ISC)`). Copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates, and the other holders named in its licence files, which are reproduced in full in section 5. <https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs>
- **aws-lc-sys 0.45.0** (declared `ISC AND (Apache-2.0 OR ISC) AND Apache-2.0 AND MIT AND BSD-3-Clause AND (Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT) AND (Apache-2.0 OR ISC OR MIT-0)`). Copyright Amazon.com, Inc. or its affiliates. All Rights Reserved, and the other holders named in its licence files, which are reproduced in full in section 5. <https://github.com/aws/aws-lc-rs> [a further licence file inside the crate is reproduced in section 5]
- **dpi 0.1.2** (declared `Apache-2.0 AND MIT`). Copyright (c) 2018 Jorge Aparicio, and the other holders named in its licence files, which are reproduced in full in section 5. <https://github.com/rust-windowing/winit>
- **ring 0.17.14** (declared `Apache-2.0 AND ISC`). Copyright (c) 2009 The Go Authors. All rights reserved, and the other holders named in its licence files, which are reproduced in full in section 5. <https://github.com/briansmith/ring> [a further licence file inside the crate is reproduced in section 5]
- **unicode-ident 1.0.22** (declared `(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Unicode-3.0`). Copyright © 1991-2023 Unicode, Inc. <https://github.com/dtolnay/unicode-ident>

- **dpi**: Apache-2.0 for the crate (text in section 4) and MIT for the code it
  takes from libm; its `LICENSE-LIBM-MIT` follows in full.
- **unicode-ident**: used under MIT for its code and Unicode-3.0 for the Unicode
  Character Database tables it embeds; both texts are in section 4.
- **aws-lc-rs**, **aws-lc-sys** and **ring**: their licence files follow in full,
  because they attribute individual parts (AWS-LC, BoringSSL, OpenSSL, SSLeay,
  fiat-crypto and others) that a summary would lose.

Also reproduced in full below:

- **libm** (listed under MIT in section 4): one licence, but its `LICENSE.txt`
  names several holders for parts ported from musl and FreeBSD.
- **Licence files below a crate's root.** Every crate in section 4 was searched
  for `LICENSE*`, `COPYING*`, `NOTICE*`, `THIRD_PARTY*` and `PATENTS*` files
  below its root. Those found are reproduced here, except:
  - `aws-lc-sys 0.45.0`: `aws-lc/LICENSE` is the same text as the crate's root `LICENSE`, apart from trailing whitespace.
  - `libsqlite3-sys 0.30.1`: `sqlcipher/LICENSE`. SQLCipher is built only with the `sqlcipher` features, which HiWave does not enable.
  - `ring 0.17.14`: `src/polyfill/once_cell/LICENSE-APACHE` is the Apache-2.0 text, which is in section 4; the once_cell code is used under MIT.
- **V8's licences**, for the code ported into the vendored Boa (section 3).

Mathematisch Centrum (CWI, see http://www.cwi.nl) in the Netherlands

## 6. In the repository, not in the shipped binary

Listed so the next inventory does not have to rediscover them. None of these
is compiled into `hiwave` or copied into an app bundle.

- **Ahem test font** (`crates/rustkit-text/tests/fixtures/Ahem.{ttf,woff,woff2}`),
  from web-platform-tests; used by tests only.
- **Noto Sans** (`baselines/common/fonts/NotoSans-*.ttf`, SIL Open Font License
  1.1); used by the parity baselines only. HiWave bundles no fonts: text is
  drawn with the fonts installed on the system.
- **Test pages and images** under `fixtures/`, `websuite/`, `static-web-suite/`,
  `cases/`, `parity-*`, `goldens/` and `baselines/`, including the MDN
  learning-area gallery image a `rustkit-image` unit test embeds
  (`websuite/js-ladder/01-mdn/32-image-gallery/images/pic4.jpg`, inside
  `#[cfg(test)]`).
- **Node packages** under `tools/parity_oracle/node_modules` (Playwright,
  pixelmatch, pngjs): developer tooling.
- **Build-time and test-time crates**: `[build-dependencies]` and
  `[dev-dependencies]` across the workspace, and the crates only
  `hiwave-mcp`, `hiwave-smoke`, `parity-capture`, `rustkit-bench` and
  `rustkit-test` use.
- **Crates in `Cargo.lock` that this build does not enable**: optional and
  target-gated dependencies such as wgpu's Vulkan and GLES back ends, the
  quinn family, and other-platform crates. They are in the lock file and not
  in the `cargo tree` output for this package on macOS.
- **Filter lists** (EasyList, EasyPrivacy): not bundled. A running HiWave
  downloads them from `easylist.to` into the user's cache
  (`crates/hiwave-shield/src/filter_lists.rs`).
- **System frameworks** (WebKit, AppKit, CoreText, Metal and the rest): part of
  macOS, linked dynamically, not redistributed.

## 7. How this file was made, and what was not verified

`scripts/third_party_notices.py` writes this file. To regenerate it, and to
check that it is current (exit 1 and a diff summary when it is not):

```bash
python3 scripts/third_party_notices.py
python3 scripts/third_party_notices.py --check
```

The crate list is the output of this, for both targets, with the lines whose
path is under `crates/` (HiWave's own) removed:

```bash
cargo tree -p hiwave-app -e normal --prefix none --format '{p}|{l}|{r}' --target <target> --locked
```

It is valid for `-p hiwave-app` with default features on the two macOS
targets. `-e normal` leaves out build- and dev-dependencies, which are not
linked. A build with other features, of another package, or of the whole
workspace at once (which unifies features across members) can link more.

Licence expressions and repository URLs are the `license` and `repository`
fields of each crate's `Cargo.toml`. Copyright lines are collected from the
`LICENSE*`, `COPYING*`, `COPYRIGHT*`, `NOTICE*` and `UNLICENSE*` files at the
root of each crate's published source (`~/.cargo/registry/src`). Licence
files below a crate's root are found by walking each crate's directory; the
script stops on one it has not been told about. The works in sections 2 and 3
were found by hand: by listing every `include_str!` and `include_bytes!` in the
workspace, and by searching `crates/`, `third_party/`, `scripts/` and `tools/`
for attribution comments ("Copyright", "SPDX", "ported from", "derived
from", "based on", "adapted from", "copied from", "taken from"). The script
does not repeat that search.

Not verified:

- Copyright lines are what each crate's own licence files say (300 crates).
  78 crates ship no copyright line; their entries give the `authors` field
  instead, which names authors, not necessarily copyright holders. Their
  upstream repositories were not read, except Boa's.
- Licence expressions are the crates' own declarations. No crate's source was
  audited file by file for code under a licence other than the declared one;
  only files named like a licence were looked for.
- Which licence to use where a crate offers a choice is a convention chosen for
  this file (stated in section 4), not something a lawyer reviewed. The same
  goes for whether pointing at upstream URLs satisfies MPL-2.0 section 3.2(a),
  and for how the Python licence applies to a port of a port.
- The vendored Boa was searched for attribution comments, not compared line by
  line with other engines. The V8 and Python notices were read from V8's
  `main` branch, not from the revision the port was made from.
- The Rust standard library's own third-party notices are pointed at, not
  reproduced.
- The list is for the macOS binary. The Windows and Linux ports resolve other
  platform crates and need their own files.
- HiWave has no packaging step in this repository; whatever builds the
  downloadable app must copy this file into it.
